title: Asynchronous prefetch orchestrator and KV cache stabilization
creator: Asha Patel
description: Objective: Replace ad-hoc synchronous prefetch logic and brittle cache mutation paths with an asynchronous prefetch orchestrator and deterministic KV cache stabilization primitives. This ticket bundles a low-level refactor (lock-free prefetch queue + bounded worker pool), a safe migration path for the on-disk KV index, and scheduler cleanup to remove a legacy blocking path that causes tail latency spikes under bursty traffic. Scope: 1) Implement an async orchestrator (task producer -> rate-limited prefetch workers -> weakly-ordered completion) that decouples ingress from cache fills. 2) Introduce a sharded LRU layer for hot keys and a compact background compaction job for KV index files. 3) Replace legacy spinlocks in the scheduler fast-path with a cooperative, sleep-aware handoff using crossbeam channels to reduce CPU spin and improve fairness. 4) Add deterministic integration tests and microbenchmarks, and a canary rollout with circuit-breaker fallback to current cache implementation.
acceptance_criteria: No regression in p50 latency on standard gen-bench (<=1% change)
p99 tail latency reduces by at least 15% under synthetic burst workloads compared to baseline
KV cache hit-rate for long-tail workloads improves or remains steady; write amplification from compaction remains within historical bounds
Async prefetch queue exposes metrics: queued, inflight, worker_saturation; dashboards created in console-2026.03
Canary rollout with automatic fallback (runtime-1.22-canary) completes with no customer errors after 48h in staging and 72h in prod-shadow
All new public symbols follow API stability policy and are feature-flagged
progress_notes: 2026-03-01: Kickoff meeting with runtime, infra, and reliability; agreed on bounded worker pool size defaults and observability signals.
2026-03-04: Prototype async prefetch queue implemented (crossbeam deque) and microbench shows 2x reduction in lock hold-time on the hot path.
2026-03-07: Found correctness issue where prefetch reordering could cause stale cache fills during rapid model-rollovers; mitigated by attaching request epoch metadata to prefetch tokens.
2026-03-09: RFC posted on Confluence (link below) detailing migration steps for on-disk index format and compaction windowing; security approved minimal I/O changes.
2026-03-11: First end-to-end test run in staging: discovered regression in memstats due to unbounded prefetch backpressure; fixed by adding bounded semaphore to producers.
2026-03-12: PR #1487 opened for orchestrator + sharded-LRU; requesting review from @sara, @doug, @yiming. Perf numbers attached to PR description.
2026-03-14: Scheduler handoff patch merged to branch runtime-scheduler-cleanup; integration tests green. Plan to enable orchestrator behind feature flag for canary next week.
rollback_plan: Feature behind runtime.flag.async_prefetch; immediate fallback to legacy prefetch path if error rate or p99 increases beyond thresholds. Ops playbook updated with diagnostics and quick toggle runbook.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Reordering in async prefetch could serve stale KV entries during model rollout. Mitigation: attach epoch tokens and validate before promotion.
Risk: Increased IO from compaction during warm-up. Mitigation: compaction windows are rate-limited and coordinated with autoscaler to avoid IO storms.
Risk: Subtle deadlocks with scheduler handoff. Mitigation: thorough fuzzing, property-based tests, and staged canary with slow ramp.
